instructions: Start in a high plank with hands slightly wider than shoulders and body in a straight line. Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at about a 45-degree angle. Pause briefly near the bottom, then press through your palms to return to the starting position. Keep your core tight and avoid sagging your hips.

Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly turned out. Brace your core and sit your hips back and down as if lowering into a chair. Keep your chest up and knees tracking over your toes. Lower until your thighs are at least parallel if mobility allows, then drive through your heels to stand back up.

Place your forearms on the floor with elbows under shoulders and extend your legs behind you. Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels. Brace your abs and glutes, and avoid letting your hips sag or pike upward. Hold the position while breathing steadily.

Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Step forward with one leg and lower your hips until both knees are bent about 90 degrees. Keep your front knee aligned over your ankle and your torso upright. Push through the front foot to return to standing, then switch sides.

Begin standing, then squat down and place your hands on the floor. Jump or step your feet back into a plank position. Perform a push-up if desired, then jump or step your feet back toward your hands. Explode upward into a jump with arms overhead, and repeat with controlled movement.

Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders. Drive one knee toward your chest, then quickly switch legs as if running in place. Keep your shoulders stacked over your wrists and maintain a strong plank position. Move at a controlled but quick pace.

Stand upright with arms at your sides and feet together. Jump your feet out wide while raising your arms overhead. Jump back to the starting position with feet together and arms at your sides. Continue at a steady rhythm, landing softly.

Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor about hip-width apart. Tighten your core and press through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees. Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower slowly back down. Avoid over-arching your lower back.

Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, using a wall or support for balance if needed. Raise your heels off the floor by pushing through the balls of your feet. Pause briefly at the top, then lower your heels slowly under control. Keep your ankles moving through a full range of motion.

muscle_groups_activated: Latissimus Dorsi, Biceps, Rear Delts, Core
instructions: Grip the bar with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, palms facing away. Start from a dead hang with shoulders engaged. Pull your chest toward the bar by driving elbows down and back. Lower yourself with control to a full hang and repeat.

Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand at chest level. Plant your feet on the floor and press the weights upward until your arms are extended without locking forcefully. Lower the dumbbells slowly until your elbows are near bench level. Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows throughout.

muscle_groups_activated: Quadriceps, Glutes, Hamstrings, Core, Lower Back
instructions: Position the barbell across your upper back and unrack it with feet about shoulder-width apart. Brace your core, sit your hips back and down, and lower until your thighs are at least parallel if possible. Keep your chest up and knees tracking over your toes. Drive through your midfoot and heels to stand back up.

Stand with your feet about hip-width apart and the bar over the middle of your feet. Hinge at the hips, bend your knees, and grip the bar with a flat back. Push the floor away as you stand, keeping the bar close to your body. Lock out by standing tall, then lower the bar with control by hinging at the hips first.

Hold the bar at upper-chest level with hands slightly wider than shoulders. Brace your core and press the bar straight overhead until your arms are fully extended. Keep your ribs down and avoid leaning back excessively. Lower the bar to the starting position under control.

muscle_groups_activated: Upper Back, Lats, Rear Delts, Biceps
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hinge forward at the hips with a slight bend in the knees. Hold the bar with arms extended below your shoulders and a neutral spine. Pull the bar toward your lower ribs or upper abdomen, squeezing your shoulder blades together. Lower the bar slowly while maintaining your hinged position.

Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand and palms facing forward. Keep your elbows close to your sides as you curl the weights toward your shoulders. Squeeze the biceps at the top, then lower the dumbbells slowly. Avoid swinging your torso or using momentum.

Hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands or one hand at a time. Keep your elbows pointed forward and close to your head as you bend them to lower the weight behind your head. Extend your elbows to raise the dumbbell back up. Keep your core braced and avoid flaring the elbows outward.

Stand with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and a slight bend in the elbows. Raise the weights out to the sides until they reach shoulder height. Lower them slowly and under control. Keep your shoulders down and avoid shrugging or swinging.

Stand tall holding a barbell in front of your thighs. With a soft bend in the knees, hinge at the hips and lower the bar along the front of your legs. Stop when you feel a stretch in your hamstrings while keeping your back flat. Drive your hips forward to return to standing.

Sit in the leg press machine with your back flat against the pad and feet placed shoulder-width apart on the platform. Unlock the safety and lower the sled until your knees bend comfortably without your lower back rounding. Press through your feet to extend your legs, stopping short of fully locking the knees. Return slowly to the starting position.

Sit on the machine with your knees aligned with the pivot point and the pad resting on your lower shins. Extend your legs until they are nearly straight, squeezing the quadriceps at the top. Lower the weight slowly back to the starting position. Keep your torso against the seat.

Sit in the machine with your knees aligned to the pivot and the pad placed against your lower legs. Curl your legs down or back by contracting your hamstrings. Pause briefly at the end of the movement, then return slowly to the start. Keep your hips pressed into the seat.

Adjust the seat so the handles line up with mid-chest height. Press the handles forward until your arms are extended without locking hard. Return the handles slowly until you feel a stretch in the chest. Keep your shoulders down and back against the pad.

muscle_groups_activated: Latissimus Dorsi, Biceps, Rear Delts, Mid Back
instructions: Sit at the lat pulldown machine and secure your thighs under the pads. Grab the bar with a wide overhand grip and pull it down toward your upper chest. Squeeze your shoulder blades down and back, then return the bar upward with control. Avoid leaning too far back or jerking the weight.

muscle_groups_activated: Mid Back, Lats, Rear Delts, Biceps
instructions: Sit with your feet braced on the platform and hold the cable handle with a neutral spine. Pull the handle toward your torso by driving your elbows back. Squeeze your back muscles at the end of the pull, then extend your arms forward slowly. Keep your chest lifted and avoid rounding your shoulders.

Adjust the seat so the handles start around ear or shoulder level. Press the handles upward until your arms are extended comfortably. Lower them slowly back to the start without losing back support. Keep your core braced and neck relaxed.

Sit on the pec deck machine with your back flat against the pad and elbows slightly bent. Bring the handles together in front of your chest by squeezing your pecs. Pause briefly, then return the arms slowly to the open position. Avoid using momentum or overextending the shoulders.

Set the pulleys at chest height and stand in the center with one handle in each hand. Step forward into a stable stance and keep a slight bend in the elbows. Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a hugging motion, then return slowly until you feel a stretch. Keep your torso steady.

Attach a straight bar or rope to the high pulley and stand with elbows tucked close to your sides. Press the handle downward by extending your elbows until your arms are straight. Pause at the bottom, then return slowly to about 90 degrees. Keep your upper arms fixed and avoid leaning forward.

muscle_groups_activated: Rear Delts, Upper Back, Traps, Rotator Cuff
instructions: Set the cable at upper-chest or face height and use a rope attachment. Pull the rope toward your face while flaring your hands apart and squeezing your upper back. Keep your elbows high and your torso stable. Return slowly to the starting position.

Stand with feet slightly wider than hip-width and hold the kettlebell with both hands. Hinge at the hips and swing the kettlebell back between your legs. Explosively extend your hips to drive the kettlebell to chest height, letting your arms guide rather than lift it. Allow it to swing back down and repeat.

Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell vertically at chest level with both hands. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and squat down by bending your knees and hips. Keep your chest upright and elbows pointed toward the floor. Push through your heels to stand back up.

Hold dumbbells at your sides and stand in front of a sturdy bench or box. Place one foot fully on the platform and drive through that leg to stand up. Bring the other foot up to meet it, then step back down with control. Keep your torso upright and avoid pushing off too much from the trailing leg.

Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and a barbell over your hips. Plant your feet firmly and drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor. Squeeze your glutes at the top and keep your chin tucked. Lower your hips back down under control.

Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back and a dumbbell in each hand. With a slight bend in the elbows, raise your arms out to the sides until they are in line with your shoulders. Squeeze your upper back, then lower slowly. Avoid shrugging or using momentum.

Sit on the floor with your knees bent and lean your torso back slightly. Clasp your hands together or hold a light weight and rotate your torso side to side. Keep your core engaged and feet on the floor or lifted if advanced. Move with control rather than speed.

Lie on your side and prop yourself up on one forearm with your elbow under your shoulder. Stack your feet and lift your hips so your body forms a straight line. Hold the position while keeping your core tight and hips from dropping. Switch sides after the desired time.

Support your body on parallel bars with arms straight and shoulders down. Lower yourself by bending your elbows until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor or as mobility allows. Press back up until your arms are extended. Keep your torso slightly forward to emphasize the chest.

muscle_groups_activated: Latissimus Dorsi, Biceps, Rear Delts, Core
instructions: Kneel or stand on the assistance platform and grip the pull-up handles. Select an assistance level that allows controlled reps. Pull your body upward until your chin is near the bar, then lower slowly to full extension. Keep your movements smooth and avoid swinging.

Place your shoulders and back against the machine pads and set your feet on the platform. Unlock the sled and lower it by bending your knees and hips. Descend until you reach a comfortable depth, then press through your feet to return to standing. Keep your back against the pad throughout.

Sit at a preacher bench with your upper arms resting on the pad and hold the weight with an underhand grip. Curl the weight upward by bending the elbows while keeping your upper arms fixed. Lower the weight slowly until your arms are nearly straight. Do not let your shoulders roll forward.

Lie on your back with your heels on a stability ball and arms on the floor for support. Lift your hips into a bridge, then pull the ball toward you by bending your knees. Extend your legs to roll the ball back out. Keep your hips elevated and core engaged.

Stand with your back against a wall and slide down until your knees are bent around 90 degrees. Keep your feet flat and your knees over your ankles. Hold the position while maintaining a neutral spine and steady breathing. Rise by pushing through your feet and sliding back up the wall.

Start in a squat position with feet shoulder-width apart. Drive through your feet to jump explosively upward, extending your hips, knees, and ankles. Land softly with bent knees and immediately lower into the next squat. Maintain balance and controlled landings.

Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding a medicine ball overhead. Brace your core and forcefully slam the ball into the ground using your entire body. Catch or retrieve it safely and repeat. Use a strong hip hinge and keep your back neutral.

Hold one end of a battle rope in each hand and stand in an athletic stance. Rapidly wave one arm up and down while alternating sides to create continuous waves. Keep your core braced and knees slightly bent. Move with quick, powerful arm actions.

Sit on the rower with feet strapped in and grasp the handle. Begin with a strong leg drive, then lean back slightly and pull the handle toward your lower ribs. Reverse the motion by extending your arms first, then hinging forward, then bending the knees. Maintain smooth, rhythmic strokes.

Sit on the air bike and grasp the moving handles. Pedal and push/pull the handles with steady, powerful effort. Increase intensity for timed intervals, then recover at a slower pace. Keep your torso stable and breathe deeply.

Step onto the pedals and hold the handles if available. Move your feet in a smooth elliptical motion while maintaining an upright posture. Adjust resistance and incline as needed for intensity. Keep your steps fluid and avoid leaning heavily on the handles.

muscle_groups_activated: Grip, Forearms, Shoulders, Core, Traps, Legs
instructions: Stand between two heavy weights and pick one up in each hand. Walk forward with tall posture, shoulders down and core braced. Take controlled steps without letting the weights swing excessively. Set the weights down safely after the desired distance or time.
